kw: Section 1 · Positioning 1.1 The idea what is being sold THE HOUR + Every existing studio in Skopje sells access: to a machine, a class, a floor. ORA offers the hour itself. What happens inside it, what happens around it, and who she is when it ends. Three things build the hour. Nothing enters this brand that doesn't belong to one of them: The Room holds it. The Movement fills it. The Woman takes it back. Side Governs Pillar Answers The Room Space, material, light, hospitality Standard Why the price holds The Movement The five disciplines, method, instructors Integration Why the category is new The Woman Who she is, what she leaves with, community Return Why she stays 1.2 The category where ORA stands First in Macedonia NO INCUMBENT + The category is Macedonia's first hybrid movement studio for women. Skopje has gyms, spin studios, and pilates studios that bolt on extras. ORA belongs to none of them. It belongs to a category that already exists in Barcelona, London and Dubai and has simply never opened here. ORA does not enter a competition, it opens one. For the woman who lives deliberately and does not compromise on standard, ORA is Macedonia's first hybrid movement studio : five

kw: Section 3 · Customer 3.1 Her the primary woman Core EARLY-MID 30s + She has already filtered everything in her life except fitness, because nothing here has met her standard. Early-to-mid thirties. She owns a small business or runs a serious one. Her circle is small and chosen. She walks Vodno, takes her coffee at Duplo or Dabov, keeps a nutritionist and a bedtime she protects. What she eats, what she reads, who she works with: all of it already decided. What she buys One hour with nothing required of her. No performing, no explaining, no being looked at. Women who speak her language. kw: Section 5 · Risk 5.1 Instructor readiness the stated risk Primary AUDITED IN HOUR ONE + The stated risk was never demand. In Angela's own words, it is whether the instructors are ready. The international-standard claim gets audited in the first hour of the first class, by a woman who already knows what that standard looks like elsewhere. It is being managed rather than watched. Instructors train under a master coach connected to an established hybrid studio in Dubai, online through the lead-up and in person before the doors open. The opening moved from September to October specifically to buy that runway. If the instructors are not ready, the date moves again before the standard does. 5.2 Four other live risks named, with the answer FOUR + The room has to hold five disciplines. The workbook describes 150 m2 as tight for four, and its equipment budget covers bikes, sound, lighting and mats, with no treadmills in it. Five disciplines, one room is the category claim, so the floor plan and the equipment list have to prove it before the claim goes to print. The credit system is unfamiliar locally. title: The name
kw: The name what ORA means ЧАС + 0 / 00 ŌRA (Latin, n.) /ˈoː.ra/ hour; a measured passage of time. ЧАС (Macedonian, n.) /t͡ʃas/ hour; class; lesson. A single word carrying two meanings at once. “ОВА Е ТВОЈ ЧАС“ in Macedonian, can be read in two ways: This is your hour. This is your class. Both are true. Every other studio in Skopje sells access; to a machine, a class, or a floor. ORA holds space for an hour that belongs entirely to you: sixty uninterrupted minutes designed to restore, strengthen, and reconnect. The hour is the canvas. Everything else exists to shape what unfolds within it. 02

title: Where it came from
kw: Where it came from the founder’s story TWO YEARS + Angela was twenty-two when leukemia put her in a hospital bed for two years. She came home at forty-five kilograms. The way back was built one movement at a time, and each discipline gave back a different part of her. None could have done the others’ work. That is the whole argument for five disciplines under one roof. The story came first and the product came out of it, in that order. 01 strength First, because she had to be able to carry herself. 02 pilates Then, when her body asked for something quieter. 03 cycling Then, when she needed to feel alive rather than merely upright. Before ORA there was HUMN, the first Macedonian activewear brand made for women, which Angela co-founded. ORA opens to a community she has already built. 03

title: The Room
kw: The Room space, material, light, hospitality Standard 150 M2 + Ninety-five minutes in the building for a sixty-minute class · one square is five minutes 15′ EARLY THE HOUR 20′ LATE Atrium Movement Room Atrium 150 m2 arranged so it behaves like four hundred One Movement Room. One Atrium. What happens between them is the part nobody else in Skopje is building. The Atrium is open to the sky, with a living tree and an oak bench. She arrives fifteen minutes early on purpose and opens her laptop. She leaves twenty minutes late because she is talking to the woman she rode beside. Music from the class carries through, and that is deliberate: the Atrium is the studio’s living room. This is Skopje’s caf ritual brought inside the brand, since coffee is already the reason people here arrive early and stay late. ORA takes that habit and puts a movement room beside it. The room is the argument. Everything else is commentary. What the room holds to How it reads on a given day Light Natural light leads, and never lands on her body. title: The Movement
kw: The Movement five doors, one practice Integration FIVE HOURS + A healthy body is not built by one discipline. 01 strength Barbell and bodyweight, heavy work, controlled reps. Low light. RnB and hip hop, loud enough to disappear into. The day she lifts what matters. 02 running Treadmill intervals, pace and breath. The day she moves fast and does not stop. 03 cycling Lights down, sound up, forty-five minutes of rhythm. Latin, RnB, hip hop. Angela on the front bike, singing. Healthy clubbing, which is her own phrase for it. 04 pilates Breath, core, control. Afro house underneath, quiet. The body learns to listen. 05 yoga Near silence. Room tone. She comes back to presence, then goes home. Her body picks the one it needs today Five doors into one practice. Every hour has its own sound. Playlists and choreography are made in-house and changed monthly, so the room never becomes a rerun. The instructor knows her name before she sits down, in every class and every discipline. 05

title: The Woman
kw: The Woman who she is, what she leaves with Return SIXTY MINUTES + Everything at ORA exists for one purpose: her. The room welcomes her. The movement challenges her. But neither is the destination. They are simply the path back to herself. She arrives carrying deadlines, expectations, responsibilities and noise. For one hour, all of it stays outside. What remains is the woman beneath it all. She doesn’t leave as someone new. She leaves as more of herself. She does not come to be fixed. She comes to come back. 06

title: Community
kw: Community different reasons, the same hour ONE PLACE + ORA was born around the belief that every woman needs time for herself, but that every woman will use that time differently. Some come for strength. Others for confidence, balance, energy, or peace. Different reasons, different stories, different lives; All coming together in the same place, for the same hour: one that belongs entirely to them.

title: Who ORA is
kw: Who ORA is the person behind the voice SPRING + Age Around thirty. Speech Speaks with intention: nothing unnecessary, every word heard. Style Her own, unmistakable. Register Serious most of the time, sharp when she is not. Around her You feel safe, appreciated, free to ask anything. Would she say this? ORA is written as a person rather than as a set of adjectives, because a person is something you can check a sentence against. Whoever is holding the phone, the pen or the microphone asks the one question above, and the answer is usually obvious inside a second. She’s not the sun. She’s not the cloud. She’s spring. 1.2

title: How ORA speaks
kw: How ORA speaks six rules SAY IT, THEN STOP + Say the thing, then stop. The instinct to add one more line of reassurance is the instinct to sound like everyone else. Describe the fact, not the feeling. The lights go down and the music comes up does more work than an unforgettable experience . She can feel things without being told to. Address her directly. You more often than we . ORA talks to one woman, never to an audience. No exclamation marks. Certainty does not need them. Never sell inside the hour. Selling happens before she arrives and at reception. Once she is in the room, nothing is being sold to her. Say women, not girls, in anything written. Spoken, in the room, warmth is the team’s own. Written, it is women. The same voice on a sign, on Instagram and at the door Short sentences, plain words. Warm, never cute. Certain, never loud. The six rules above are the whole of it, and they hold in Macedonian as well as in English, since none of them is about vocabulary. A caption, a signage plate, a reply to a message and a sentence said at reception all come out of the same mouth. 1.3

title: The words
kw: The words ours and never ours TWO LISTS + The lexicon · both lists set the same size, so only the wording separates them Ours Your hour · room · return · movement · community · rhythm · method · honest · real · earned · felt · built · here · now · hers · ours · healthy clubbing · coming back to yourself. Never ours Ready to crush your goals. Transform your body. Snap back. Beast mode. Bikini season. Emoji-stacked captions. Countdown urgency. Anything that turns her body into a project she is failing Every phrase on the right shouts at her, and most of them tell her the body she walked in with is the thing to be fixed. Countdown urgency and emoji stacks belong to the same instinct: they treat her attention as something to be taken rather than earned. The left-hand list is eighteen words long and stays that way, since a voice is a set of words used often enough to become recognisable. Section 2 · Naming and language 2.1

title: How ORA names things
kw: How ORA names things plain nouns SIX NAMES + The current roster · every permanent thing ORA has a name for 01 the Atrium 02 the Movement Room 03 the ORA Index 04 the First Hour Booklet 05 the Member Card 06 ORA HUMN English for what a thing is, Macedonian for what it means Plain nouns throughout. The ORA prefix is for permanent things only, which is why the Index and the Member Card carry it and a promotion or a month never will. No invented compounds: no ORAfit, no ORAlife, no ORAmove. Disciplines are called what they are, and one-word marketing names belong to the studios ORA is defined against. Named this Never this strength running cycling pilates yoga RIDE, SCULPT, BURN the ORA Index, the ORA Member Card ORAfit, ORAlife, ORAmove 2.2

title: Two languages
kw: Two languages which language, which surface MK / EN + Macedonian carries feeling · English carries function Македонски The promise on the door The welcome The message after her first class Anything said to her rather than about the studio English Discipline names The timetable The app interface Wayfinding Never translated Ова е твој час. Never translated, ever The mark Pick the language for the sentence and finish it there Ова е твој час is the one line that only works in Macedonian, and translating it destroys the double meaning. The mark is a placed file in every language. Everything English on the list is a word she already recognises from the studios she follows, which is the test: if she has to learn a word to use the timetable, the timetable is wrong. The two are never mixed inside a single sentence. 2.3

title: Explaining credits
kw: Explaining credits a language problem Revenue TWELVE CLASSES + The same offer, twice · the second one sells Wrong Buy a 12-credit package and redeem across disciplines. Right Twelve classes. Use them on anything. Cycling one day, yoga the next. Never lead with the word credits Most women in Skopje have only ever bought a flat monthly gym fee. Credits are unfamiliar, and unfamiliar costs money at the point of sale. The fix is language, not a discount, so lead with classes. If she asks a second question, the answer is always the same shape: she is buying classes, not access, and no discipline is locked behind a different payment. One membership. Any of the five. You choose on the day. 2.4

title: Approved copy
kw: Approved copy use as written EIGHT LINES + The copy bank · the surface labels it, the line is the specimen The door Ова е твој час. Website hero One room for every way she moves. Instagram bio Hybrid movement studio for women. Strength · running · cycling · pilates · yoga. Central Skopje. A nervous first-timer Welcome to the room where the noise of the day stops mattering for an hour. The mood line Welcome to the studio where your mood picks the movement. Intro offer Three classes. Any three. See if the room is yours. After her first class You came. That was the hard part. Bring a friend Bring her once. The room does the rest. If a surface needs something new, it is written to match these Use the eight as written rather than as a starting point. The Macedonian-facing lines should be written in Macedonian by Angela rather than translated from English, since a translated welcome always sounds translated. Section 3 · At the door 3.1

title: Before she arrives
kw: Before she arrives the schedule FIFTEEN NAMES + The schedule is not a list. It is fifteen women’s names, each with a small story we already know. The brand is audited here more than anywhere else This section is Angela’s own protocol, held as written. The team already knows she is coming. The booking system gives reception every name on the day’s schedule by the hour, and the front desk reads the names at the start of the shift. They know who has been here before. They know who is new. 3.2

title: The first three seconds
kw: The first three seconds room, silence, person IN THAT ORDER + 01 The room Light from the Atrium falls into the entrance. The concrete is warm. No fluorescent strip. The air smells faintly of cedar, with no commercial cleaner and no incense. 02 The silence Not the silence of an empty space, the silence of a considered one. Music is playing below the threshold of being noticed. 03 The woman at reception Not behind a counter that hides her. Not on her phone. She is reading, or making a note, or arranging the tray of Member Cards. The first thing she notices is the room The order is the point. Reception comes third, after the light and the quiet have already done their work. The moment the door opens, whatever the woman at the desk was doing turns into attention on whoever has walked in. This is the first message of the brand. The room was waiting for you. The person was here, present, before you arrived. 3.3

title: The greeting
kw: The greeting word for word FIRST TIME + First time, word for word Hi. You found us. Are you Marija? Welcome, I’m Pavlina. Come in. Let me show you around before we start. Her name, then the team’s name, then the room Two lines, and each does one job. The first says she was expected. The second gives her a name to use back, and moves straight into the walkthrough so she never has to stand and decide what happens next. 3.4

title: The walkthrough
kw: The walkthrough sixty seconds WE DO NOT POINT + In the Atrium This is the Atrium. You can wait here before class, there’s a smoothie bar if you want something. After class this is where most of the women stay for fifteen, twenty minutes. Some bring their laptops in the mornings. The light is good here all day. At the Movement Room glass That’s the Movement Room. All five disciplines happen in there: strength, running, cycling, pilates, yoga. Each one has its own time. Today is cycling. The bikes are set up. At the changing rooms Changing rooms are down the hall. Lockers on the left. Showers on the right. Towels are ready for you. Sixty seconds, ninety if she is slow We walk her through, and we do not point. The walkthrough does three things at once. It gives her geographical certainty, so she never has to ask. It shows her everything has been thought of before she needed it. And it establishes the Atrium and the Movement Room as two different places with two different jobs, before she has used either. 3.5

title: In the room
kw: In the room the instructor HER NAME + The instructor knows her name before she sits down. Every class, every discipline. Greet the woman next to you The instructor greets the women already there, asks how the last class went, and introduces the new woman by name. During class she goes to each woman individually for position and posture. After a well-executed series she uses the phrase greet the woman next to you , which is how strangers in a dark room become a community without anyone announcing it. 3.6

title: Leaving
kw: Leaving the smoothie, the question SAME TIME TOMORROW + At the door, reception looks up after her Are you joining us same time tomorrow? Her smoothie is already being made She ordered before class and reception remembered. Reception remembers what she has, and remembers when she changes her mind. The question at the door is the last thing she hears, and it assumes she is coming back. Section 4 · The line 4.1

title: What ORA refuses
kw: What ORA refuses five refusals FIVE + Nothing we would not put in our own bodies. No colour, material or finish that does not belong to the brand. Not for a sponsor, not for a season. No one who treats this as a job. Skill can be trained. Arrogance cannot be removed. We do not compete on price. If price is the objection, the answer is the room. We do not become mass. The finite funnel is a constraint we accept, not a problem we widen our way out of. Every one of these costs money to keep That is what makes them refusals rather than preferences. The sponsor with a budget, the talented instructor with a temper and the quiet week in July are the tests, and they arrive in the first year. The answer to all three is written above, so that nobody has to invent one under pressure. ORA / BRAND CHARACTER <section

title: VISUAL SYSTEM LOGIC
kw: 01 VISUAL SYSTEM LOGIC + 1 / 00 1' 5' 15' 30' 60' One hour. Sixty minutes. A measure of time that becomes the foundation of the visual system. We translate the structure of an hour into a visual language, using its divisions, rhythm and proportions as the basis of the system. The grid here is adopted rather than designed: it already exists inside the hour. We measure in minutes rather than millimetres. Every distance on every surface is a duration: a margin is one minute, a text column is a quarter of an hour, an image runs half past. Change the format and the millimetres change, but the minutes never do. This is what allows a poster, a screen and a wall to remain the same object. The grid is the hour laid flat, and every surface is a sixty-minute class drawn at a different size. The field is sixty squares across and one square is one minute. The margin is one square, regardless of the surface. The squares group into columns the way the face groups minutes: twelve columns of five, or six of ten. title: LOGO
kw: 02 LOGO Downloads + Construction 60 60 minutes 45° 30 30 minutes Hour clock holds the hour clock becomes ORA’s mark Play The visual system begins with the measure of an hour. The logo gives that measure a physical form: the clock, a structure designed to hold it. In the same way, ORA exists to hold an hour entirely for her, creating the space for that time to belong to her. ORA adopts this structure as its mark, turning the idea of holding time into a visual symbol. Logo variations The Clock The symbolic expression The Clock is the distilled symbol of ORA and the most direct visual expression of its central idea. It can be used independently as a recognisable brand mark, or paired with the slogan to create a more conceptual expression of the brand. Its simplicity allows it to live across both small and large scale applications, from digital touchpoints to the physical environment. SVG PNG PDF The Frame The structural expression The Frame extends the ORA mark into a graphic structure. title: ART DIRECTION
kw: 05 ART DIRECTION Downloads + ONE SYSTEM, FIVE EXPRESSIONS ORA's art direction starts with one shared visual system: the red, the two faces, typography and the field. The five disciplines are not given separate identities. Instead, the same elements are used in different ways: changing in scale, placement, weight and intensity. This makes each discipline feel distinct while keeping everything clearly part of ORA. strength controlled / grounded running propulsive / repetitive cycling cyclical / repetitive pilates precise / controlled yoga held / fluid TYPE CREATES THE RHYTHM Type gives each discipline its own sense of movement. Weight represents physical load, moving from Black for Strength to Light for Yoga, while tracking opens as the intensity decreases. PT Mono is used as data: a label paired with its value, and placed directly into the field rather than kept in a fixed information block. Its position changes with the movement of each discipline: Strength clusters and holds, Running moves across the field, Cycling gathers around a centre, Pilates follows precise lines, and Yoga uses only two points and leaves the rest open.
